quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: You hear a siren while driving but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
Slow down. Do not stop until you see the vehicle.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren nearby but cannot see the emergency vehicle, pull to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure the vehicle is not coming toward you.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
The combination can make the effects of the alcohol or medicine much stronger.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can make the effects of the alcohol or medicine much stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with other drugs can increase how much both substances affect your body. For example, one drink with a cold medicine can affect you as much as several drinks would alone.

questions.question: What should you do when passing other vehicles?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane when you can see the front of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Bicycle store nearby.
Soft shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows where bicycles cross or ride near the road. Drive carefully in this area because bicycles often cross or travel beside traffic.

questions.question: Is driving at night more or less dangerous than driving during the day?

options.text: Less dangerous.
No more or less dangerous.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. It is harder to see, headlights can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the dividing line is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?

options.text: Rectangle.
Square.
Circle.
Octagon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon.
questions.explanation: Stop signs have eight sides (octagon shape). This shape is used only for stop signs. All eight-sided signs mean you must stop before proceeding.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should reduce speed to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell you to slow down. The new speed limit takes effect at the sign, not at a future sign.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, pulling from a curb, or merging is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Unnecessary.
Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic. Also always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to check if it is safe.
Turn your head and look out the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look out the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window when backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems ahead without emergency stops. Emergency stops can cause the driver behind you to crash into your vehicle.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed in both directions.
Passing is not allowed.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during the day only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic on the other side is moving toward you. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: Which traffic light means you should slow down and be careful at an intersection?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, look both ways, and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
The road ahead has many turns and curves.
More traffic is coming ahead.
There is a steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. In wet conditions, slow down, avoid sudden braking or turning, and increase the space between you and the car ahead.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly in which conditions?

options.text: Flat areas
Curved areas
Sunny areas
Shaded areas

questions.correctAnswerText: Shaded areas
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, be careful on shaded roads near trees or buildings. These areas freeze faster and dry slower than sunny areas.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction. You may only cross these lines to turn left or to pass pedestrians, cyclists, or scooter riders when it is safe.

questions.question: If another person is injured in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away right away.
Never move the injured person.
Avoid moving the injured unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid moving the injured unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move the injured unnecessarily, as improper handling can make minor injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Drive slowly through the intersection.
Stop and then go when the road is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
Turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: Unless a sign says otherwise, a red arrow means come to a complete stop and stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
Work crew ahead.
Side road.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a sharp turn ahead. Reduce your speed when you see it.

questions.question: What should you do if your tire blows out?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not use your brakes right away.
Slow down gradually and pull off the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, take your foot off the gas and do not use your brakes right away. Slow down gradually, then gently apply the brakes and pull off the road.

questions.question: What causes many crashes?

options.text: Drivers going too fast for conditions.
Drivers checking their mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
Drivers keeping a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers go too fast for the conditions. Always obey the speed limit and slow down when conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line in the road mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
You cannot pass.
You may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means both directions can pass. You may only pass if it is safe and you will not hit oncoming cars.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is passing you?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal the other driver when it is safe to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to help them pass safely.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Keep right when another driver passes you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed so the passing car can move back into the right lane easily.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is now 20 mph.
A reduced speed zone is starting.
There are more pedestrians ahead.
The reduced speed zone has ended.

questions.correctAnswerText: The reduced speed zone has ended.
questions.explanation: Follow the school zone speed limit during the times shown. An "End school zone" sign marks where the lower speed limit ends.

questions.question: How should you look to reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night?

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are too bright, look at the right side of the road ahead. Do not look directly at the headlights because the glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: What lights should you use if you stop on the road at night?

options.text: Turn off all lights.
Use parking lights only.
Use headlights only.
Turn on emergency flashers and leave low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and leave low beams on.
questions.explanation: If you stop on the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beam headlights on. This helps other drivers see your car clearly.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Use a different route.
Drive the same as you would on dry roads.
Stay farther behind other cars.
Avoid bridges and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. Your car will take longer to stop in these conditions.

questions.question: When can you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When it would interfere with other traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When a car ahead of you breaks down.
When passing on the right side of a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would interfere with other traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do it safely without interfering with other traffic.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: Possible speeds for the area.
The fastest or slowest speed you are allowed to drive.
The speed to drive in heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in bad conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest speed you are allowed to drive.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the fastest or slowest legal speed for that road. The maximum limits are for perfect conditions. You must slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: A traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Brake hard to stop immediately.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Get ready to stop before the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: Driving faster makes your tires less effective.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Shallow water is more dangerous than deep water.
Slowing down makes the road more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving faster makes your tires less effective.
questions.explanation: When you drive fast on a wet road, your tires cannot wipe away the water. Your tires may lose grip and hydroplane, causing your car to slide on the water.

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Have large blind spots.
Stop faster than regular cars.
Do not need extra space to turn or move.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have blind spots in front, on the sides, and in back. Stay away from these areas. Trucks need more space to turn and stop than regular cars because of their size and weight.
